summary: Client-side maxConnections and synchronized retries causing apparent inference slowdown and intermittent timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden increase in end-to-end inference latency and sporadic 504/timeout errors beginning 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC. Symptoms look like slow responses rather than model overload. Impact: NovaPay's payment verification flow saw degraded user experience — median latency doubled and p95 spiked to >5s for short prompt calls. Environment: Dedicated customer tenant in prod-us-east, traffic peaked ~600 rps. SDK: Java SDK v2.1.8 used in a connection-pooled service with default config except maxConnectionsPerHost was manually set to 8. Observed first: 2026-03-09 18:12 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run synthetic load from the customer's service with many short-lived requests (concurrent clients ~200, each making 3req/s). 2) SDK configured with maxConnectionsPerHost=8, retry policy: immediate retry, maxAttempts=3, no jitter. 3) Observe client-side queueing and long tail in request latencies. Observed behavior: - Clients reported queueing on socket acquisition; internal SDK metrics show connection pool saturation with avg wait time ~200ms and occasional spikes >1s. - Gateway logs show many short-lived connections and many HEADERS frames with RST_STREAM shortly after. - Serving runtime logs show stable CPU/GPU utilization and normal token service times, indicating backend inference not saturated. - Correlated times show retry bursts aligned with prior request timeouts. Hypothesis: Misconfigured maxConnectionsPerHost (too low for concurrency pattern) created an application-level bottleneck for socket acquisition. Coupled with aggressive, synchronized retry behavior (no backoff/jitter), this caused coordinated retry bursts that amplified perceived latency and produced transient 504/timeouts at the edge. Local evidence: - SDK client thread dump from app shows many threads blocked on connection pool wait. - tcpdump shows many repeated SYNs and short-lived connections. - API gateway reported increased connection churn and transient 502/504 responses. Logs attached: - Gateway traces: trace ids start with 0a7b-... - SDK metrics: connection_wait_ms histogram peaked at 1200ms. Temporary workaround provided to customer: - Increase SDK maxConnectionsPerHost to 64 and enable exponential backoff with jitter on retry policy OR revert to SDK v2.1.6 which has a slower default retry. - Add a short client-side circuit breaker for persistent timeouts. Next steps: - Engineering to reproduce in lab (Omar Ruiz) and validate the retry/backoff patch. - SRE to add a synthetic check for connection wait latency per tenant. - Support to coordinate rollback/patch with NovaPay and confirm metrics returned to baseline. Root cause analysis (provisional): Combination of under-provisioned client connection pool and synchronized immediate retries created a client-side queueing bottleneck that manifested as perceived inference latency; server-side resources were healthy. Resolution notes: Patch landed in SDK to enable jittered exponential backoff by default and expose better pool sizing guidance in README (PR #422). Infra tweak: API gateway tune to increase http2 stream concurrency per upstream for dedicated tenants. Customer remediation: NovaPay applied SDK config changes and observed latency return to baseline within 30 minutes. Follow-ups: - Add new doc in SDK repo about recommended maxConnectionsPerHost per qps pattern. - Add a support runbook for detecting retry storms via connection_wait_ms and gateway connection churn.
